chunks: He عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to say:

Whoever restrains himself for an obligatory salat (prayer), waiting for its time, then performs it at the beginning of its time, completing its ruku' (bowing), its sujud (prostration), and its khushu' (humble attentiveness), then glorifies Allah, Mighty and Majestic, magnifies Him, and praises Him until the time of another salat (prayer) enters, and does not engage in idle speech between them, Allah will write for him the reward like that of the one performing hajj (pilgrimage) and the one performing 'umrah, and he will be among the people of 'Illiyyin.

key_terms.رُكُوعَهَا: its bowing, performed properly within the salat (prayer)
key_terms.سُجُودَهَا: its prostration, performed completely within the salat (prayer)
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: the highest elevated ranks of the righteous in the hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying obligatory prayers at their earliest time and remembering Allah between them?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages careful devotion to the obligatory salat (prayer), especially performing it at its earliest time with complete ruku', sujud, and khushu'. It also praises remaining engaged in dhikr between prayers and avoiding idle speech, promising immense reward and a lofty rank in the hereafter.
